name: Memorial Hall of the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea
funding: A state memorial built in 1958 and moved to its site in 1993. Closed in December 2014 for a centrally approved expansion, it reopened in September 2020 with free admission.
watch: The 182,000 square metre site has a 53 metre tower and a national defence education park; 12 million visits before the 2014 closure.

propaganda.summary: Built by the state in 1958 as China's only Korean War museum and listed as a national patriotic education base in 1997. Expanded on central approval, it reopened in 2020 for the war's 70th anniversary.

name: Memorial of the Site of the First National Congress of the CPC
funding: The Shanghai Party committee bought the site in 1952 and shows it free. The state built the hall across the street, opened by Party secretary Li Qiang in June 2021.
watch: Xi Jinping took the Politburo Standing Committee there in October 2017 to renew the Party oath; China Daily counts 12 million visits since June 2021.

propaganda.summary: The Shanghai Party committee bought the Party's birthplace in 1952 and opened it as a memorial, named a national patriotic education base in 1997; a tripled memorial hall opened for the 2021 centenary.

name: Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution
funding: A People's Liberation Army institution, a deputy corps-level unit under the General Political Department, whose propaganda bureau supervises it. Admission is free; the state rebuilt it from 2012 to 2017.
watch: One of the Ten Great Buildings, opened 1 August 1960; since the 2017 rebuild, 159,000 square metres, 43 halls and over 160,000 relics.

propaganda.summary: The Central Military Commission approved the PLA museum in 1959 and it opened in 1960 under the General Political Department. The Central Publicity Department named it a national patriotic education base in 1997.

name: Museum of the Communist Party of China
funding: Built on a 2017 Communist Party Central Committee decision, with support from the National Development and Reform Commission, Finance Ministry and Beijing city. Entry is free.
watch: Opened 18 June 2021. Xinhua reported more than 3.5 million visits by 30 June 2024.

propaganda.summary: The Party Central Committee decided in 2017 to build it. People's Daily, the Party paper, reports the Central Propaganda Department led construction. Xi Jinping called it a spiritual home for Party members, China Daily reports.

name: Museum of the War of Chinese People's Resistance Against Japanese Aggression
funding: Budget unit in the Beijing government's published accounts: 809 million yuan of public funding in 2025, 711 million of it project spending.
watch: Inside Wanping Fortress near the Marco Polo Bridge. Beijing opened a patriotic education base there for Hong Kong and Macau youth in August 2025.

propaganda.summary: Mitter (China Quarterly, 2000) says Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Qiaomu authorized it and that it shapes official memory legitimizing Party rule. A patriotic education base for Hong Kong youth opened there in 2025.

name: Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall
funding: Founded 1985 by the Nanjing Municipal Government; the Jiangsu provincial government added a research institute in 2016. The Standard reported about 6 million visitors in 2025.
watch: The Victory Exhibition Hall opened 7 December 2015. Admission is free with prior registration.

propaganda.summary: The Nanjing municipal government built it in 1985. Emily Matson (Wilson Center) finds its phases track the Communist Party's changing legitimizing narrative. Contested Histories reports state-defined aims, including patriotic education.

name: National Museum of China
funding: Funded by China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism as a level-1 public welfare institution. The Art Newspaper counted 7.4 million visitors in 2019.
watch: Formed 2003 by merging the Museum of the Chinese Revolution and the National Museum of Chinese History. Building opened 1959.

propaganda.summary: Reviewing Denton's study, Joseph Allen says official ideology has driven Chinese museums since 1949. Time found the 2011 Road to Rejuvenation display sanitized and pro-government. Xi Jinping gave his Chinese Dream speech there in 2012.

name: Yan'an Revolutionary Memorial Hall
funding: A state museum founded on 1 July 1950, rated a national first-class museum by the National Cultural Heritage Administration in 2008. Admission free since the building opened in August 2009.
watch: The building holds over 38,000 relics and draws nearly 4 million visits a year; Xi Jinping took the Politburo Standing Committee there in October 2022.

propaganda.summary: The state founded the hall in 1950 to display the Party's Yan'an years and listed the Yan'an sites as national patriotic education bases in 1997; Xi took the Politburo Standing Committee there in 2022.

name: National Memorial on Vítkov Hill
funding: Property of the Czech Ministry of Defence since 1 June 2024, administered by the Military History Institute Prague. From 2000 to 2024 the National Museum ran and renovated it.
watch: Built 1928 to 1938 by Jan Zázvorka for the Czechoslovak legionaries, with the Unknown Soldier's tomb; state ceremonies and military parades are held there.

propaganda.summary: After 1948 the Communist Party made the memorial its pantheon; the Central Committee opened the Klement Gottwald Mausoleum there in December 1953, run by an Interior Ministry department until the body was cremated in 1962.

name: Arktikum (Regional Museum of Lapland and Arctic Centre)
funding: Houses the city-owned Regional Museum of Lapland and the University of Lapland's Arctic Centre. In 2025 the museum spent EUR 1.75M; admissions brought EUR 1.0M and state museum funding EUR 507,621.
watch: The museum counted 172,661 visits in 2025, most of them paid; the building is shared with a university research centre.
records_note: Figures are in the Finnish Heritage Agency's museum statistics; the building's owner was not found.
